taxonomy.note: Accepted by Kew/POWO. Texas has substantial infraspecific complexity; the learner remains species-level but preserves the need to check local varieties and segregate species such as M. stanfieldii.
taxonomy.texas_taxonomic_note: Turner's Texas treatment recognized five M. punctata varieties in Texas and treated former varieties fruticulosa, maritima, and stanfieldii as distinct species.

evidence: BONAP/NAPA provides a county-level native distribution map for Monarda punctata and is the project's primary range cross-check.
Travis County — UT Plant Resources Center's Travis County Lamiaceae herbarium index explicitly includes Monarda punctata var. intermedia.
Tom Green County — a peer-reviewed Texas field study lists Monarda punctata as a sampled host plant in Tom Green County among naturally collected host-associated populations.
Bexar County — Smithsonian entomological records document females of Mesoxaea texana collected at flowers of M. punctata in sand dunes of southeast Bexar County.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Because M. punctata has multiple Texas varieties and overlaps with the Texas endemic M. stanfieldii complex, ambiguous garden/seed-mix observations are not used for county proof. PASS is based on BONAP plus independent regional specimen/field records from three target-zone counties.

morphology.look_here_first: Look for the combination of pale cream-to-yellow flowers densely spotted purple plus pale white/pink/lavender bracts that are pointed but NOT long-bristle-tipped. Then inspect the calyx mouth: in M. punctata it remains open and is only ciliate, rather than being plugged by dense white hairs as in M. stanfieldii.
diagnostic_traits: aromatic annual, short-lived perennial, or perennial depending on variety; stems four-angled and usually hairy
leaves opposite, generally lanceolate to linear-lanceolate, with low serrations
inflorescence usually 1–4 or up to several separated dense flower whorls/verticils
showy subtending bracts are white to pinkish or purplish, often with green toward the tip
bract tips acute to acuminate but not drawn into the long bristles characteristic of M. citriodora
calyx tubular; teeth short, deltoid/triangular to triangular-lanceolate and ciliate rather than long-bristle-tipped
calyx mouth in typical M. punctata is open and ciliate, an important separator from M. stanfieldii
corolla cream or pale yellow, strongly bilabiate, usually conspicuously spotted purple/reddish-purple
fruit divides into four smooth nutlets

confusers.separator: M. citriodora usually has purple bracts and long bristle tips on both floral bracts and calyx teeth; M. punctata has pale bracts without long terminal bristles and short triangular/lanceolate calyx teeth.

Critical Central Texas confuser: M. stanfieldii has the calyx mouth closed by a dense plug of white/silvery hairs, while M. punctata has an open calyx mouth that is merely ciliate. This character remains useful on dried material.
M. fistulosa has pink/lavender flowers in a more conventional dense terminal head and lacks the signature cream/yellow, heavily spotted corollas plus tiered pale bracts of M. punctata.

diagnostic_roles: side view of stacked flower whorls
pale floral bract macro showing pointed non-bristle tip
calyx-tooth macro showing short triangular/ciliate teeth
calyx-mouth macro showing open ciliate opening
opposite leaves and square stem node
photo_verification.provenance_note: Prefer diagnostic macro views that show the calyx mouth and bract tips. The user's iNaturalist example is a study-photo lead; public-reuse licensing must be verified photo-by-photo.
